Build a detset from glatos detections or an actel preload

Source: R/read_detset_from.R
read_detset_from.Rd

Reads detections that another package holds into a detset, so work started in glatos or actel can continue here.

Usage

read_detset_from(x, receivers = NULL)

Arguments

x

A glatos_detections data frame or an actel preload list.

receivers

Optional. With glatos input, a glatos receiver table. With actel input, the receivers attribute of the to_actel() result.

Value

A detset.

Details

glatos. x is a glatos_detections data frame, or any data frame with its columns detection_timestamp_utc, receiver_sn, transmitter_codespace, transmitter_id and animal_id. station_id is station where present, else glatos_array. The animals table is built from the animal columns GLATOS exports repeat on every row. Deployments come from receivers, a glatos receiver table (as from glatos::read_glatos_receivers()). Without it they are inferred: one per receiver and station, from its first detection to one second after its last, at the first position the detections give. Inferred deployments say nothing about when a receiver listened without hearing anything, so the log says they were inferred.

actel. x is the list actel::preload() returns. Detections are the ones actel kept, those of the tags in its biometrics; actel's time stamps are moved back to UTC from its study area time zone. animal_id is the biometrics' animal_id column where it has one, as to_actel() writes, and the transmitter code otherwise. actel keeps receivers as whole numbers, and names a receiver deployed more than once "number.dpl.k" for its k-th deployment; the suffix is dropped on the way back. Give receivers = attr(a, "receivers"), the lookup that to_actel() returned as a, to restore receiver_serial and receiver_model. Without it receiver_serial holds actel's number, and the log says so.

The first log record is the one detset() writes; a second, from this function, names the source and its row counts.

See also

to_glatos(), to_actel()

Examples

study <- detqc_example
dets <- detset(study$detections, study$deployments, study$animals)
glatos_dets <- to_glatos(dets)
from_glatos <- read_detset_from(glatos_dets)
writeLines(strwrap(detset_log(from_glatos)$reason[2], width = 72))
#> read from glatos detections: 3,297 detections, 14 deployments (inferred
#> from the detections), 4 animal rows
